questions.question_text: How many members serve on the South Dakota Real Estate Commission?
questions.explanation: The commission has five members appointed by the Governor — three active real estate brokers and two members of the public (SDCL 36-21A-13). Members serve three-year terms and may not serve more than three consecutive full terms.

questions.question_text: A newly appointed SDREC commissioner is a licensed broker. Of the other four current members, two are brokers and two are public members. Is this appointment valid?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, three brokers and two public is correct
distractors: No, only two brokers may serve at once
No, the majority must be public members
Yes, but only if from a different party
questions.explanation: Three active brokers and two public members is exactly what the statute requires, so the appointment is valid (SDCL 36-21A-13). The party restriction is separate: all five members may not belong to the same political party.

questions.question_text: Which restriction applies to the political party membership of SDREC commissioners?
questions.correct_answer: All five may not be from the same party
distractors: At least three must be from the majority party
No more than two from any single party
Commissioners must be registered as independent
questions.explanation: All five members may not be of the same political party (SDCL 36-21A-13). Nothing requires an even split, so a four-to-one majority is fine — only a unanimous single-party commission is barred.

questions.question_text: Under SDCL 36-21A, which activity falls within the SDREC's jurisdiction?
questions.explanation: The commission licenses and disciplines property managers alongside brokers, broker associates, auctioneers, residential rental agents, and home inspectors. Property manager is a restricted broker's license issued under SDCL 36-21A-47. Mortgage rates, tax assessments, and zoning belong to other agencies.

questions.question_text: The SDREC operates under which state department?
questions.explanation: The commission is an adjunct of the Department of Labor and Regulation but keeps all of its own functions, including administrative ones (SDCL 36-21A-16). It must report to the secretary of labor and regulation at least annually.

questions.question_text: Who appoints members to the South Dakota Real Estate Commission?
questions.explanation: The Governor appoints all five members — three active brokers and two public members (SDCL 36-21A-13). Each serves a three-year term, and no member may serve more than three consecutive full terms (SDCL 36-21A-14).

questions.question_text: A consumer complains that a home inspector provided a negligent report. Which entity has authority to investigate?
questions.explanation: Home inspectors are licensed and registered through the commission, so a complaint about a negligent inspection goes to the SDREC. The commission also covers brokers, broker associates, property managers, auctioneers, and residential rental agents.

questions.question_text: The SDREC learns that an unlicensed person is selling real estate for compensation. What is the Commission's enforcement route?
questions.correct_answer: Ask a court for an injunction
distractors: Issue a cease and desist order
Refer the matter to the Division of Insurance
questions.explanation: The commission must go to court for an injunction against anyone practicing real estate without a license, and the court awards it attorney fees and investigation costs (SDCL 36-21A-91). Its cease and desist power reaches only subdivision sales violations.

questions.question_text: In addition to licensing real estate practitioners, the SDREC also registers which types of projects?
distractors: Commercial office buildings and retail spaces
questions.explanation: Time-share projects register with the commission annually, condominium developers file a notice of intent and must wait for the commission's public report before selling, and subdividers need a subdivision certificate. All three clear the commission before units reach the public.

questions.question_text: A broker associate wants to know which powers the SDREC does NOT have. Which is correct?
questions.correct_answer: The SDREC cannot set commission rates
distractors: The SDREC cannot set education standards
questions.explanation: The commission licenses, investigates, disciplines, and sets education standards, but it does not set commission rates — those are negotiated, and fixing them would violate antitrust law. State law expressly preserves each licensee's right to set his or her own fees (SDCL 36-21A-68).
